title: Polyconvexity does not imply true-stress-true-strain monotonicity in the incompressible three-dimensional case
summary: We study constitutive conditions of hyperelastic potentials for incompressible material behavior in three dimensions. By means of a counterexample, we show that polyconvexity does not imply true-stress-true-strain monotonicity. Thus, polyconvexity alone is not strong enough to guarantee a physically reasonable response for idealized elasticity.
